expectations.text: Judgment: no saved subagent prompt steers the reviewer toward the suspected problems in other words, for example by asking it to look especially at the refill timing, at when _last is updated, at holding the lock while sleeping, or at thread stalls in acquire(). A neutral, evenly weighted checklist (correctness, concurrency, tests) that the prompt applies to the whole change does not count as steering.
expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5] The only prompt sent to the reviewer is subagent-prompt-04.md. It names no suspected problem: "Code-review main..feature/token-bucket (f7f6429..3050047) ... against the Ask, Scope and Decisions of .cadence/workstreams/token-bucket-review.md@262862b (read it with `git show ...`; do not read its Notes section)." Its only other guidance is general: "Back every finding with a repro command and its raw output, or mark it UNPROVEN. Also list what you didn't check." The Scope it points to sets a neutral standard for the whole change (subagent-prompt-01.md): "Standard: correctness, thread-safety and test adequacy of the change; no written spec exists in the repo." The user's hunches about _last and the lock held across the sleep appear only under "## Notes (not for reviewers)" in subagent-prompt-01.md, and that prompt goes to a scribe who is told "Do not read or analyse the code itself." The prompt that does spell out the hunches, subagent-prompt-05.md ("Verify or refute two claims ... (1) 'the refill clock drifts...' (2) 'the lock is held across the sleep in acquire()...'"), goes to a separate verifier (verifier-1, task hunch-check), not to the reviewer (reviewer-1, blind-review). subagent-prompt-02.md, 03.md and 06.md are about bookkeeping only (the tasks file, commits, recording results), and 06.md was sent after the review finished. Caveat: the reviewer is pointed at a file that contains the Notes and is only told not to read them. So whether the review stayed blind depends on the reviewer obeying, but the prompt text itself does not steer.
